# Figwig v1 conformance fixtures

These seven small files are generated by the upstream Figwig fixture generator
at commit [`c0e5d6522c677b9f03cd6831e2dbcea759866628`](https://github.com/jmschrei/figwig/tree/c0e5d6522c677b9f03cd6831e2dbcea759866628)
(Python package version 0.2.0). The original fixture generator and independent
specification reader are preserved in `scripts/vendor/` with their MIT license.

Run ordinary JavaScript conformance tests without Python or network access:

```sh
npm test -- test/conformance
```

Regenerate the files and their independent oracle from the repository root:

```sh
uv run --python 3.12 --with-requirements scripts/requirements-fixtures.txt scripts/generate-fixtures.py
```

The original generation environment was Python 3.12.13, NumPy 2.5.4, Numba
0.68.0 and llvmlite 0.50.0. The dependency file pins the exact upstream source
commit and Python dependencies. Compressed bytes may vary with system zlib,
but numerical values and their expected representations remain deterministic.

`expected.json` records provenance, file SHA-256 checksums, metadata, statistics,
summary and zoom records, sparse chromosome signals, and deterministic queries
(seed 271828). Its signal values come exclusively from the independent
`format_reference.py` implementation. The generator checks **every base of every
track** against Python's `FigWigReader(verify=True)` before writing the oracle.
No JavaScript decoder participates in generation. `NaN`, infinities and negative
zero have explicit string representations; numeric values use JSON numbers.
All represented integer values are within JavaScript's exact integer range.

The four original toy fixtures have identical genomic signals; appended and
merged files share a second signal dataset with an added `late` track. The
oracle deduplicates these signals and omits implicit zero entries. Its per-file
metadata and index expectations remain distinct.

| File | Layout and purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `zlib.fw` | Position order, zlib and stored chunks, several runs per group, zooms |
| `stored.fw` | Position order, uncompressed, no zooms |
| `tracks.fw` | Track order, uncompressed blocks |
| `tracks_zlib.fw` | Track order, compressed blocks |
| `appended.fw` | Appended track; historical tables/index remain as unused bytes |
| `merged.fw` | Merged equivalent; historical structures removed |
| `blocks.fw` | Multiple blocks on a 200 kb chromosome; implicit-one block |

Together they exercise dense, sparse, matrix and runs chunks, element codes
0–8 (uint8/16/32, int8/16/32, float32, implicit one and float64), missing values,
chromosome edges, heterogeneous group values, stored chunks inside a compressed
file, summaries and zoom levels. The toy files contain 1,215 tracks, most empty;
that is deliberate coverage of matrix chunks with very sparse track presence.

Tile summaries omit NaNs and round each tile sum to float32. Zoom records sum
those float32 tile sums into float64 values. Therefore summary values are tested
against the Python summary oracle rather than an assumed exact full-resolution
sum, and cannot by themselves provide missing-aware mean denominators.
